content_voiceover: Let's walk through management of beta thalassemia, which boards love to test. Think of it in four buckets. First, conventional therapy: transfusion targeting a pre-transfusion hemoglobin of nine to ten grams per deciliter, using leukodepleted blood, plus iron chelation, splenectomy, and HbF-modulating agents like hydroxyurea. Second, endocrine support for the downstream complications of iron overload, so sex hormone, thyroid, and growth hormone replacement, plus fertility agents and osteoclast inhibitors for bone disease. Third, curative stem cell transplant from a matched related, matched unrelated, or cord blood donor, reserved for transfusion-dependent thalassemia major or severe TI. Fourth, novel therapies, which are increasingly high yield. Know two by name and mechanism. Mitapivat is a pyruvate kinase R and PKM2 activator, dosed 100 milligrams twice daily, which in the ENERGIZE trial improved hemoglobin response in over forty percent of non-transfusion-dependent patients versus under two percent placebo, and in ENERGIZE-T reduced transfusion burden and achieved transfusion independence. Luspatercept is a recombinant activin receptor IIb fusion protein that traps GDF-11, reduces SMAD signaling, and promotes erythroid maturation, cutting transfusion burden by over a third in transfusion-dependent disease. Also remember gene therapy targeting BCL11A, plus hepcidin modulators and TMPRSS6 inhibitors on the horizon.
keypoints: 4 pillars: conventional therapy, endocrine support, HSCT, novel agents
Transfusion target Hb 9-10 g/dL + chelation + HbF modulators
Luspatercept: activin receptor IIb-IgG fusion, traps GDF-11, ↓transfusion burden >33%
Curative: HSCT (matched related/unrelated/cord) for TDT or severe TI
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, remember mitapivat activates pyruvate kinase and boosts hemoglobin response in non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia, while luspatercept traps GDF-11 through the activin receptor pathway to cut transfusion burden by a third in transfusion-dependent disease. Hematopoietic stem cell transplant remains the only curative option, typically reserved for transfusion-dependent or severe intermedia disease. Conventional care still means a hemoglobin target of nine to ten with chelation to prevent iron overload.
